# Frank Tindle

> IT, facilities and operations director. Thirty-one years running the
> operational half of growing businesses. Available from 6 October 2026 for
> interim and fractional engagements, and the right permanent role. Currently
> London / Guildford-based, UK, and open to relocating. Remote, hybrid or on-site all work.

## Summary

Frank Tindle is an IT, facilities and operations director with 31 years in the
video games industry, across multiple BAFTA-winning studios, most recently
IT & Facilities Director at Supermassive Games (2010-2026). Available from
6 October 2026. Open to IT Director, Operations Director and Head of IT roles
on an interim, fractional or permanent basis, and to advisory arrangements.

## Bring him in when

- You have bought something, or been bought: post-acquisition integration of
  systems, sites, suppliers and security. Five deals, both sides of the table.
- You have to get smaller without service falling over: headcount, sites and
  run rate coming down together, handled directly and decently.
- You are moving, merging or handing back buildings: fit-outs to a fixed date,
  moves with no lost working days, dilapidations run in-house.
- Your vendor costs have drifted: audit actual usage, build the evidence,
  renegotiate.
- Security has to stand up to someone else's scrutiny: a publisher, acquirer
  or insurer sends the questionnaire and the capability has to be real.
- The back office should be using AI and is not: a working group, a short list
  of dull jobs worth automating, and a human check before anything sends.

Engagement shapes: a fixed piece of work with an end date; a day or two a week
as operations or IT director; full-time interim cover during a hire; or
permanent.

## Career

- **Supermassive Games Ltd** (2010-2026): IT Manager (2010-2018), Head of Facilities and IT
  (2018-2021), then IT & Facilities Director reporting to the CEO (2021-2026). Joined at 30
  employees; the studio grew to a multi-site group peaking at 387 staff (400+ people supported,
  including around 20 at partner sites in Kyiv and Lviv), peak turnover
  of £39.1M (FY2022), and was acquired by Nordisk Games (Nordisk Film) in July 2022.
  Built the operations function from a standing start to a team of 16, covering IT,
  workplace support, facilities, physical and cyber security, events and
  procurement. Operating budget grew from £200K to a peak of £6M. Member of the
  Senior Leadership Team. Through the industry-wide contraction, ran the function
  down from 16 to 9 as the group went from 387 people to 172 at the end of 2025, across
  redundancy rounds in February 2024 (about 90 roles) and July 2025 (36 roles); a third
  round, of up to 75 roles, followed in August 2026, shortly before he left, taking the
  studio below 95 people. Service
  held at or above HDI and Gartner benchmarks and staff satisfaction at 96-100%.
- **Criterion Software Ltd / Electronic Arts Inc** (2000-2008): Head of IT, then Head of
  Operations, then Studio IT Manager, then Senior Manager, IT Services. Dual responsibility to Criterion Games
  (Burnout franchise - three BAFTAs for Burnout 3: Takedown in 2005) and the RenderWare
  middleware business. Criterion was Canon-owned until EA's £40M acquisition in 2004;
  led the IT integration covering Guildford, Derby, Paris, Austin and Tokyo, 300+ employees,
  with no disruption to game releases. Earlier, on the buying side: when Criterion
  acquired MathEngine he merged its systems and data into Criterion's (staff were offered
  moves to Guildford and the office closed); when it acquired Data Path Ltd in Derby he
  became accountable for that site's IT and facilities and mentored its staff.
- **Iguana Entertainment Ltd / Acclaim Entertainment Inc** (1995-1999): Manager, MIS
  and Operations (1995-1997), then Director of Operations (1997-1999) at Acclaim
  Studios Teesside. Built a unified email system across sites in New York, Austin,
  Utah and the UK.

## Selected results

- Took the whole studio from an office-only, no-VPN culture to home working in
  March 2020: 90%+ connected inside two weeks, every in-scope machine encrypted
  inside five.
- Consolidated three sites into one (2023-2025): 210+ people moved in a single
  day; dilapidations delivered at £195k against a £211k budget.
- Delivered a 17,000 sq ft fit-out to a fixed date in 2022 when the network
  supplier quoted 99-150 day lead times against a 76-day window.
- Cut one software renewal from $109k to $76k by rationalising seats on usage
  data; found about £80k of wrong or unnecessary kit in a single £145k quote.
- Built a security awareness programme that returned a 0.7% phishing click rate
  studio-wide against a Gartner benchmark of around 15%; commissioned the
  studio's first penetration test; completed a major publisher's 118-question
  security assessment to deadline.
- Stood up three development sites in Ukraine in five months and kept them
  running through the 2022 invasion.
- Re-homed a cloud subscription in five working days when the supplier ceased
  trading, with no fees and the reserved-capacity discount intact.
- Automated weekly IT service report built with Claude and the Freshservice MCP:
  live ticket data, AI-drafted narrative, human-reviewed before sending,
  benchmarked against HDI and Gartner.

## Areas of expertise

Post-acquisition integration (five deals across three decades, two as the buyer and
three as the acquired business; four
corporate parents - Canon, Acclaim, EA, Nordisk Film - spanning SME to enterprise),
scaling operations through rapid growth, org design and workforce change through
both growth and contraction, office moves and estates, business continuity,
cyber and physical security, procurement and vendor management, and applying AI
to back-office work. The experience is from games; none of it is specific to games.
